title: Dedicated capacity request escrow and scheduling protocol
creator: Ananya Rao
description: Define a formal protocol for handling dedicated capacity reservation requests that balances strict throughput guarantees with fleet efficiency. This ticket covers an 'escrow' concept for short-term soft commitments, a scheduling window model for start/end times, rules for converting escrow -> hard reservation, and how autoscaling/burst credits interact with escrowed capacity. Goal: reduce contention and over-provisioning while enabling customers to request predictable throughput bands and scheduled bursts.
acceptance_criteria: Protocol doc with state machine and terminal states (requested, escrowed, confirmed, fulfilled, cancelled)
Confluence playbook with step-by-step approval matrix and SLA bindings for each state
API contract additions documented for reservation lifecycle (fields added: escrow_token, schedule_window, burst_credit_policy)
E2E test plan that simulates concurrent escrowed requests and validates allocation fairness and SLO preservation
Implementation plan with rollback criteria and telemetry signals defined (allocation-failure-rate, preemptions, buffer-utilization)
comments: 2025-02-14 - Ananya Rao: Created initial ticket after customer workshop (customer X and Y requested scheduled bursts for end-of-month jobs). Key ask: guaranteed throughput windows and ability to queue short notice requests without overcommitting.

2025-02-18 - Liam Chen: Drafted state machine sketch: requested -> escrowed (soft commit) -> confirmed (hard commit) -> active -> fulfilled/cancelled. Escrow expires after configurable TTL or when converted to confirmed by ops/automated policy.

2025-02-21 - Design review (Maya Patel): Recommended visualizing schedule windows on Console calendar; suggested clarifying difference between 'burst credits' and 'burst capacity' in UX copy. Action: design to add microcopy and calendar slot validation.

2025-02-25 - Eng sync (Suhail Reddy): Raised concern about race conditions when multiple escrowed requests overlap on same node class. Proposed solution: escrow lanes (soft reservations) with probabilistic admission and fallback routing to lower-tier models.

2025-02-28 - PM note: Agreed to conservative default: escrow TTL = 72h, auto-confirm threshold = 24h before start, and max burst factor = 2x baseline for confirmed reservations. Need legal to review SLA wording for 'throughput band'.

2025-03-01 - Security (Priya Menon): Requested security_review_required flagged and KMS annotation for escrow tokens; ensure tokens are short-lived and auditable. Added as dependency to security review.

2025-03-03 - Data/Observability (Diego Alvarez): Added telemetry items: escrow_to_confirm_rate, avg-time-to-confirm, conflict-resolution-count, buffer-utilization-per-fleet. Will add dashboards (link to staging dashboard once PR merged).

2025-03-04 - Liam Chen: Implementation plan attached in PRs. Next steps: finalize API contract, schedule integration spike (2d) with autoscaler to validate burst-credit accounting under concurrent requests.
notes_on_tradeoffs: Escrow provides flexibility but increases scheduling complexity; default conservative TTL to limit leakage.
Hard guarantees require buffer lanes which reduces utilization; to mitigate we propose dynamic buffer sizing based on historical adherence and customer SLAs.

Autoscaling interaction: prefer pre-warm (confirm->allocate) vs on-demand scaling for confirmed windows. Pre-warm increases cost but improves cold-start latency; decision: provide both and surface cost/latency tradeoffs in console during booking.
Fleet controls: maintenance draining may preempt soft commitments; include preemption policy that favors confirmed reservations and migrates escrowed tenants to best-effort variants.
next_steps: Finalize API spec and publish client SDK changes (target 2025-03-10)
Integration spike with autoscaler and quota manager (2d) and report findings
Design calendar UI mocks and validate with two pilot customers
